§29.12(i) Elliptic-Function Form

ⓘ
Keywords:
Lamé functions, Lamé polynomials, elliptic-function form, notation, periodicity, relation to Lamé functions, relations to Lamé polynomials, zeros
Notes:
See Arscott (1964b, Chapter 9).
Referenced by:
§29.14, §29.6(i)
Permalink:
http://dlmf.nist.gov/29.12.i
See also:
Annotations for §29.12 and Ch.29

Throughout §§29.12–29.16 the order ν in the differential equation (29.2.1) is assumed to be a nonnegative integer.

The Lamé functions 𝐸𝑐νm⁡(z,k2), m=0,1,…,ν, and 𝐸𝑠νm⁡(z,k2), m=1,2,…,ν, are called the Lamé polynomials. There are eight types of Lamé polynomials, defined as follows:

where n=0,1,2,…, m=0,1,2,…,n. These functions are polynomials in sn⁡(z,k), cn⁡(z,k), and dn⁡(z,k). In consequence they are doubly-periodic meromorphic functions of z.

The superscript m on the left-hand sides of (29.12.1)–(29.12.8) agrees with the number of z-zeros of each Lamé polynomial in the interval (0,K⁡), while n−m is the number of z-zeros in the open line segment from K⁡ to K⁡+i⁢K′⁡.

The prefixes u, s, c, d, 𝑠𝑐, 𝑠𝑑, 𝑐𝑑, 𝑠𝑐𝑑 indicate the type of the polynomial form of the Lamé polynomial; compare the 3rd and 4th columns in Table 29.12.1. In the fourth column the variable z and modulus k of the Jacobian elliptic functions have been suppressed, and P⁡(sn2) denotes a polynomial of degree n in sn2⁡(z,k) (different for each type). For the determination of the coefficients of the P’s see §29.15(ii).

§29.12(ii) Algebraic Form

ⓘ
Keywords:
Lamé polynomials, algebraic form
Notes:
See Arscott (1964b, §9.3.2).
Permalink:
http://dlmf.nist.gov/29.12.ii
See also:
Annotations for §29.12 and Ch.29

With the substitution ξ=sn2⁡(z,k) every Lamé polynomial in Table 29.12.1 can be written in the form

29.12.9 ξρ⁢(ξ−1)σ⁢(ξ−k−2)τ⁢P⁡(ξ),
ⓘ
Symbols:
k: real parameter, ξ=sn2⁡(z,k): substitution, (0 or 12): parameter ρ, (0 or 12): parameter σ, (0 or 12): parameter τ and P⁡(ξ): polynomial
Referenced by:
§29.12(ii), §29.12(iii)
Permalink:
http://dlmf.nist.gov/29.12.E9
Encodings:
TeX, pMML, png
See also:
Annotations for §29.12(ii), §29.12 and Ch.29

where ρ, σ, τ are either 0 or 12. The polynomial P⁡(ξ) is of degree n and has m zeros (all simple) in (0,1) and n−m zeros (all simple) in (1,k−2). The functions (29.12.9) satisfy (29.2.2).

§29.12(iii) Zeros

ⓘ
Keywords:
Lamé polynomials, applications, electrostatic interpretation, physical, zeros
Notes:
See Whittaker and Watson (1927, §23.46) and Arscott (1964b, §9.2.1).
Referenced by:
§29.19(ii)
Permalink:

Let ξ1,ξ2,…,ξn denote the zeros of the polynomial P in (29.12.9) arranged according to

29.12.10 0<ξ1<⋯<ξm<1<ξm+1<⋯<ξn<k−2.

29.12.11 g⁡(t1,t2,…,tn)=(∏p=1ntpρ+14⁢|tp−1|σ+14⁢(k−2−tp)τ+14)⁢∏q<r(tr−tq),
ⓘ

g⁡(t1,…,tn): function (locally)

29.12.12 0≤t1≤⋯≤tm≤1≤tm+1≤⋯≤tn≤k−2,

29.12.13 ρ+14ξp+σ+14ξp−1+τ+14ξp−k−2+∑q=1q≠pn1ξp−ξq=0,
p=1,2,…,n.
ⓘ
Symbols:
n: nonnegative integer, p: nonnegative integer, k: real parameter, (0 or 12): parameter ρ, (0 or 12): parameter σ, (0 or 12): parameter τ and ξn: zeros
Referenced by:
§29.20(iii)

This result admits the following electrostatic interpretation: Given three point masses fixed at t=0, t=1, and t=k−2 with positive charges ρ+14, σ+14, and τ+14, respectively, and n movable point masses at t1,t2,…,tn arranged according to (29.12.12) with unit positive charges, the equilibrium position is attained when tj=ξj for j=1,2,…,n.
